about.title: About Karigar
about.subtitle: Empowering traditional Indian artisans through technology, dignity, and direct global access
about.missionDesc1: Karigar is India's premier digital sanctuary dedicated to protecting, promoting, and celebrating genuine handcrafted heritage. We bridge the gap between generational rural master craftspeople and mindful connoisseurs worldwide.
about.missionDesc2: By eliminating predatory middlemen, offering real-time regional voice assistance in local dialects, and providing 100% blockchain-verified Geographical Indication (GI) tags, Karigar ensures every rupee spent directly honors the creator.
about.quote: “When you support a Karigar, you support a legacy.”
about.value1Desc: Transparent pricing, direct escrow payouts, and 0% hidden commission fees.
about.value2Desc: Every piece certified with government Pehchan identity and regional GI badges.
about.value3Desc: Artisans can list and manage products using their voice in their mother tongue.
about.value4Desc: Fair-trade escrow protects buyers until delivery, and guarantees instant artisan payout.

home.heroSubtitle: Direct from India’s master craftspeople to your sanctuary. Verified Geographical Indication provenance, protected by fair-wage artisan escrow.
home.cartographyDesc: Select a region to discover indigenous craft traditions, master weavers, and active sovereign preservation mandates.

home.ramdasBio: Master of Kadwa and Katan silk techniques. Keeper of 18th-century Persian jaal draught cards.
home.ananyaBio: Reviving narrative Nakshi Kantha tapestries depicting traditional agrarian folklore and flora.
home.ismailBio: 16-stage resist block dyeing using wild pomegranate, river mud, and fermented scrap iron.
home.ghulamBio: Weaving coded 'Talim' manuscripts into whisper-soft Changthangi cashmere goat fleece.

puducherry.description: Franco-Tamil enclave of handmade paper, terracotta figures, and natural dye batik.

wb-nk-042.name: Radha-Krishna Narrative Nakshi Kantha Tapestry
wb-nk-042.description: Smt. Ananya Devi (National Award '18). Hand-stitched running stitch on unbleached wild tussar silk depicting Krishna under the Kalpavriksha tree.

longStory.title: The Song of the Kadamba Bough
longStory.text: Embroidered over 180 uninterrupted dawns upon hand-beaten wild tussar silk, this singular narrative revives the pastoral divinity of Radha-Krishna under the Kalpavriksha (the eternal wishing tree). Every figure is meticulously shaped by microscopic running kantha stitches, layered to create tactile low-relief ripples across the cloth.

wb-jamdani-01.name: Nilambari Fine Cotton Jamdani Saree
wb-jamdani-01.description: Master Weaver Debabrata Pal. Supplementary weft geometric and floral motif on gossamer 200s high-count handspun cotton muslin.

longStory.title: Shadows on Gossamer Muslin
longStory.text: Jamdani weaving is an intangible cultural art form where intricate floral motifs are inserted thread-by-thread into the sheer cotton warp using delicate non-mechanized bamboo needles.

wb-swarna-02.name: Mythological Swarnachari Silk Saree
wb-swarna-02.description: Master Artisan Ruma Pramanik. Gold and crimson silk brocade recreating Mahabharata battle scenes across the pallu.

longStory.title: Chariots Woven in Gold Filament
longStory.text: Swarnachari sarees inherit the epic narrative traditions of Bishnupur, featuring pure gold-plated metallic thread brocading of Mahabharata and Ramayana scenes.

wb-terracotta-03.name: Panchmura Long-Neck Terracotta Heritage Horse
wb-terracotta-03.description: Master Potter Baidyanath Kumbhakar. Hand-thrown and wood-fired natural clay votive horse with hollow segmented neck.

longStory.title: The Votive Earth of Panchmura
longStory.text: The Panchmura terracotta horse is the world-renowned symbol of Indian folk craft, handcrafted by traditional Kumbhakar artisans.

jk-pashmina-01.name: Royal Shahus Kani Weave Pashmina Shawl
jk-pashmina-01.description: Master Weaver Ghulam Hassan Mir. Hand-woven on traditional looms using Changthangi grade-A pashmina with Kani wooden needles.

longStory.title: Whispers of the Changthang Plateau
longStory.text: Hand-woven using wooden bobbins called Tujis according to coded Talim notation scripts passed down through generations in Srinagar.

rj-bluepottery-01.name: Jaipur Blue Pottery Royal Floral Urn
rj-bluepottery-01.description: Master Artisan Kripal Singh Studio. Clay-free quartz frit pottery with Persian cobalt blue arabesque painting.

longStory.title: The Turquoise Flame of Amber
longStory.text: Jaipur Blue Pottery is unique as it uses no clay, made instead from Egyptian paste of powdered quartz stone and glass.

up-chanderi-01.name: Imperial Gold Zari Chanderi Silk Tissue Saree
up-chanderi-01.description: Master Weaver Ramdas Ansari. Sheer silk-cotton woven with pure tested gold zari motifs.

longStory.title: Glimmer of the Malwa Kingdom
longStory.text: Chanderi weaving creates lightweight translucent fabrics embellished with delicate gold and silver zari buttis.

gj-ajrakh-01.name: Ajrakhpur 16-Stage Natural Dye Block Print Stole
gj-ajrakh-01.description: Shilp Guru Dr. Ismail M. Khatri. Natural indigo, madder, and iron-resist block print on Tussar silk.

longStory.title: Symphony of River and Mud
longStory.text: Ajrakh is a complex 16-step block printing process utilizing natural minerals and vegetable dyes in Kutch.

tn-kanchi-01.name: Kanchipuram Heavy Crimson Korvai Silk Saree
tn-kanchi-01.description: Master Weaver Murugan Swamy. Interlocked Korvai weave with 3-ply Mulberry silk and certified gold zari.

longStory.title: The Temple Looms of Kanchi
longStory.text: Korvai is the ancient temple technique of interlocked weaving where the border and body are woven separately and joined with unmatched strength.

cg-dhokra-01.name: Bastar Bell Metal Lost-Wax Dhokra Tribal Procession
cg-dhokra-01.description: Master Craftsperson Budhram Jhoria. Ancient cire-perdue lost-wax cast bell metal sculpture depicting tribal musicians.

longStory.title: Molten Bronze of the Bastar Forest
longStory.text: Dhokra metal casting uses the 4,000-year-old lost-wax technique, ensuring that every single figurine is a one-of-a-kind original.

up-banarasi-01.name: Varanasi Royal Katan Silk Kadwa Jaal Brocade Saree
up-banarasi-01.description: Ustad Ramdas Ansari (Padma Nominee). Pure Katan silk with gold Zari Kadwa weaving of Mughal jaal motifs.

longStory.title: The Gold Filaments of Kashi
longStory.text: Kadwa is the painstaking technique of weaving each motif individually into the silk fabric without any loose threads on the reverse.

od-pattachitra-01.name: Raghurajpur Palm Leaf Pattachitra Tale of Dashavatar
